open_points.subject: ownership rule for cross-cutting decisions A22, A26 and A28
open_points.text: “Each accepted decision has one primary owner” conflicts with A22, A26 and A28 being assigned to “cross-cutting” and with “no module holds a mechanism the others call.”
open_points.question: Are A22, A26 and A28 exceptions whose implementations are independently owned by every applying module, or must each have one owning module or shared mechanism?
options: Each applying module owns its local implementation
Create one primary owning module for each decision
Name one existing module as owner and the others as consumers
open_points.default_guess: Treat the specific cross-cutting paragraph as an exception and make every applying module own its local implementation.

witness.initial: Two use-case modules must apply A22 when opening transactions.
events: One implementer follows “Each accepted decision has one primary owner” and introduces a shared transaction-guard module.
Another implementer follows “no module holds a mechanism the others call” and duplicates the guard in both use-case modules.
outcomes: The use cases acquire a new dependency on a shared owner.
The use cases contain independent guard implementations and no shared dependency.
witness.observer: A later module or code author sees different dependency graphs and extension points.

open_points.subject: HTTP request-body model ownership
open_points.text: `models` owns “the request models,” while `api` owns “request-body models.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the definitions and validation of staff, administrator and producer HTTP request bodies?
options: `models` defines them and `api` only decodes/uses them
Split request models by route family, with an explicit boundary
open_points.default_guess: Put the shared frozen request types in `models` and make `api` their consumer.

witness.initial: A malformed staff-account creation body reaches the HTTP boundary.
events: One code author defines and validates `StaffAccountCreateRequest` in `models`, which `api` imports.
Another defines an API-local request class and maps it to a separate model value.
outcomes: There is one shared request type and one validation location.
There are two shapes and a mapping boundary whose ownership and validation precedence were not specified.
witness.observer: API clients see potentially different validation errors and generated schemas; maintainers see different module dependencies.

open_points.subject: repository port ownership
open_points.text: `models` owns “the repository interfaces,” while each repository section says it “Owns” its named repository port, such as “The `AuditRepository` port” and “The `ExpenseRepository` port.”
open_points.question: Do repository interface definitions belong to `models`, with repository modules owning only implementations, or does each repository module own both its port and implementation?
options: `models` owns all port interfaces; repository modules own SQLite implementations
Each repository module owns its port and implementation; `models` owns only exchanged records
Split data-only protocol types from behavioral port interfaces explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Keep the interfaces in `models` because repository modules are declared to know `models` and `models` precedes them in the dependency order.

witness.initial: An application module needs the `ExpenseRepository` abstraction while `portal_store` must construct its SQLite implementation.
events: One implementer places the interface in `models` and imports it from both modules.
Another places it in `expense_repository`, following that module's `Owns` statement.
outcomes: Application-facing port types remain in the first dependency layer.
Callers must import the concrete repository module or duplicate/re-export the port, changing the declared dependency boundary.
witness.observer: Application and persistence implementers see different legal imports and interface locations.

open_points.subject: producer project-scope authorization
open_points.text: `service_identity` owns “A12 … bearer authentication and producer scope” and exposes `authorize_producer_scope`, while `authorization_guard` owns “the guard part of … A12,” including “project scope … producer grant,” and exposes `authorize_snapshot_import`. The guard cannot import the later `service_identity` module.
open_points.question: Which operation is authoritative for producer scope, and what distinct responsibility remains for the other authorization capability?
options: `service_identity.authorize_producer_scope` checks scope and the guard consumes trusted evidence of that decision
Both recheck scope, with the required order and transaction boundary stated
open_points.default_guess: Make `authorization_guard.authorize_snapshot_import` the sole operation-time scope check and limit `service_identity` to principal, credential and grant lifecycle.

witness.initial: An active granted producer has authenticated for project P.
events: An administrator revokes its grant for P.
The pending import proceeds to its scope check.
outcomes: If the guard owns and re-reads scope, the import is classified as `unknown_project` and is not accepted.
If an earlier `service_identity` scope decision is trusted as sufficient, the import can still be accepted after revocation.
witness.observer: The producer sees rejection versus acceptance, and administrators see different snapshot and audit records.

open_points.subject: expense validation versus project authorization ordering
open_points.text: A7 requires recognition status and contract version to be checked before capability and active-project checks, but `expense_intake` does not know `authorization_guard`; `api` knows both yet “Must not own … a business rule.”
open_points.question: Which module orchestrates the required interleaving of recognition validation and project authorization without violating the exhaustive `Knows` lists?
options: Split a public pre-validation capability from `expense_intake`, then let an orchestrator call the guard and completion step
Change the declared order so `api` may authorize before calling `expense_intake`
open_points.default_guess: Add `authorization_guard` to `expense_intake` and let the owning use case enforce A7's complete order.

witness.initial: A valid staff session and assignment exist, project P is archived in Registry, and the submitted recognition has an unsupported contract version.
events: The staff member submits expense creation for P.
outcomes: If `expense_intake` applies A7 first, it rejects the unsupported version without asking Registry.
If `api` performs the available guard call first, Registry is queried and the archived-project failure occurs before contract-version validation.
witness.observer: The Registry operator can observe whether a validation call occurred, even though the HTTP error body is concealed.

open_points.subject: ordering of the staff progress-photo list
open_points.text: A27 has primary owner `derived_views` and no consumers, but `photo_management` owns “the order of the staff photo list it returns”; `photo_management` may not know the later `derived_views` module.
open_points.question: Who owns the staff-list application of A27, and is `photo_management` a consumer of A27 or the owner of a separate ordering decision?
options: Add `photo_management` as an A27 consumer and require the same normative ordering
Move staff-list projection and ordering to `derived_views`
Declare and own a distinct staff-photo ordering policy
open_points.default_guess: Add `photo_management` as an A27 consumer and require its staff list to use the same A27 ordering.

witness.initial: Two photos have the same `photo_date`, but their `published_at` order is opposite their `photo_id` order.
events: Staff requests the photo list through the `photo_management` path.
A viewer requests the overview gallery through `derived_views`.
outcomes: If both consume A27, both lists break the tie by `published_at` and then id.
If the ownership table is treated as exhaustive, only the overview is governed by A27 and the staff list requires an independently guessed tie-break.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers can see the same photos in different orders.
